newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo police question woman-basher, fear copy-cats.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo police question woman-basher, fear copy-cats.

text.p: Tokyo police are holding a man who confessed to bashing about 30 young women in the face while riding past them on his bicycle, but fear copy-cat attackers may still be at large, a police spokesman said on Tuesday.
A Tokyo Metropolitan Police spokesman said Yuji Sugita, 20, confessed to the attacks on Monday following his arrest on August 9 on an unrelated attempted murder charge.
"Sugita gave a written statement yesterday that said he had committed around 30 attacks in which he struck lone women in the face with bats, concrete blocks and metal bars," he said.

"He said he committed the crimes out of frustration because he had debts of around 2.5 million yen ($21,500)," the spokesman added. "The details he gave match exactly the circumstances of three attacks and we are currently investigating the rest."

Attacks have continued since Sugita's arrest, however, and Tokyo and Saitama prefectural police are still searching for copy-cat attackers they believe responsible for several of the 50 or so assaults reported since last October, the police spokesman said.
"We are maintaining our warning to single women to keep up their vigilance. There is a strong possibility that one or more copy-cat attackers are still at large," the Tokyo police spokesman said.
Victims have suffered deep cuts to the face, broken cheekbones and broken noses in attacks during the past ten months, most of which have targeted young women.
The attacks usually happened in the late afternoon or evening on deserted streets where women were either walking or cycling alone. ($1=116 yen)
